question: V tradičnom slovenskom kroji ste už z diaľky spoznali, či je žena slobodná alebo vydatá. Slobodné dievčatá mali vlasy odkryté. Čo dostala nevesta na svadbe na hlavu a nosila to potom celý život?
source_excerpt: the čepiec (bonnet), which was used by all women to tie up their hair on the back of their heads once they were married

extra.why_interesting: Slovaks see kroje at festivals and in museums, but few people think of the headwear as a public 'marital status' sign. The word 'čepčenie' is something everyone has heard, so players can work out the answer and enjoy that moment.
extra.verification_notes: Married women (brides after the wedding) wore the čepiec while only unmarried girls had free hair; regional variants like šatka exist but čepiec is the standard answer.

explanation: Pri obrade čepčenia nevieste sňali z hlavy partu a nasadili jej čepiec. Odvtedy už vlasy na verejnosti neukazovala.

question: Niektoré košele majú na cípoch goliera malé gombíky. Vymysleli ich preto, lebo hráčom istého športu golier pri cvale na koni plieskal do tváre. O aký šport išlo?
topic: Prečo vyzerá oblečenie tak, ako vyzerá
source_excerpt: polo players invented in the late 19th century to keep their collars from flapping in the wind

extra.why_interesting: Nearly every Slovak office worker owns a shirt with tiny buttons on the collar tips and assumes they are just decoration. They actually come from a fast sport on horseback. The stem gives enough footholds (wind, galloping) to reason the way there.
extra.verification_notes: Widely documented origin story: English polo players buttoned collar points to stop them flapping in their faces, and Brooks Brothers adopted it (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polo_shirt).

explanation: Pán Brooks z firmy Brooks Brothers videl anglických pólistov, ktorí mali golier pripnutý ku košeli, a tak začal šiť košele s gombíkmi na goliere. Firma ich dodnes volá „originálna pólo košeľa“.
